---
title: "Cyclotron coasting and acceleration"
description: "Track a proton through PSI sectors, mirrored trim coils and discrete RF gaps."
audience: user
status: experimental
last-reviewed: "2026-09-06"
---

The `545-add-cyclotron-coasting-beam` development branch introduces
`CYCLOTRONSECTOR` and named `TRIMCOIL` definitions. The first validation case is a
single 72 MeV proton in the PSI Ring, with magnetic fields only and no space charge.

```text
TC1: TRIMCOIL, TYPE="PSI-BFIELD-MIRRORED",
     RMIN=4.350, RMAX=4.470, BMAX=1.4E-3, SLPTC=600.0;
SM0: CYCLOTRONSECTOR, FMAPFN="bfield.dat", SYM=8,
     RMIN=1.9, RMAX=4.7, VMIN=-0.05, VMAX=0.05,
     BSCALE=1, TRIMCOIL={"TC1"}, X=3.3, Y=0, Z=0,
     THETA=0, PHI=0, PSI=0;
```

`FMAPFN` accepts the legacy PSI Ring median-plane format, with its angular origin
at zero. `SYM` must match the map's angular span. Explicit `RMIN/RMAX` must match
the file bounds; omitting them uses those bounds. Radii and vertical limits are
metres, magnetic strength is tesla, and placement angles are radians.
`BSCALE` multiplies the base map only. Eight occurrences share the loaded map.

The sector pose is the entrance tangent at the map midpoint radius
`Rm=(RMIN+RMAX)/2`. Its local ring centre is `(-Rm,0,0)`, the ring plane is X-Z,
and Y is vertical. For an identity enclosing frame, sector k is placed at
`X=Rm*cos(k*2*pi/SYM)`, `Z=Rm*sin(k*2*pi/SYM)`, `THETA=-k*2*pi/SYM`.
The existing placement resolver composes these poses with the enclosing RING
source frame. If that frame is translated to the launch radius, subtract that
translation from the sector positions to retain the same global magnet centres.

`TRIMCOIL` is a list of named definitions. Only `PSI-BFIELD-MIRRORED` is currently
implemented. Its shape radii do not impose hard cutoffs: the profile has tails.
`SLPTC` is in inverse metres; old OPAL's `0.6` in inverse millimetres becomes `600`.
Coils cover the full azimuth and should be referenced by every sector.

Assemble the sectors into a `RING` and use `RUN, TURNS=1`. Turns count directed
reference-particle crossings of the launch plane, not the nominal geometry
circumference. Tracking stops at the first timestep endpoint past the crossing;
reduce `DT` to reduce this overshoot. Explicit `TURNS` requires one timestep
segment and currently rejects checkpoint restart. The step budget remains a
safety limit; failure to return is reported as an error.

The reproducible input is `sandbox/cyclotron/opalx/coasting72.in` in the source
repository. Run it from that directory. `sandbox/cyclotron/compare_coasting72.py`
runs strictly one-rank timestep comparisons against old OPAL RK4 and LF2 orbit
dumps. Old OPAL's default is RK4; explicitly select `TIMEINTEGRATOR="LF2"` for
the matched Boris/leapfrog comparison. The supplied `reference72` input files
select each integrator explicitly. Tune extraction is deferred.

## First-turn RF acceleration

The feature branch also supports an experimental `RFCAVITY, TYPE="SINGLEGAP"`
radial voltage-profile kick for one unpolarized, median-plane proton on one rank.
Only cyclotron sectors and these gaps may occur in the line; restart is rejected.
Use `FIELDSOLVER, TYPE=NONE`.

`FMAPFN` identifies a normalized voltage/derivative profile, not a 3D map.
`VOLT` is in MV, `FREQ` in MHz and `PHI0` in degrees. For this model, `RMIN` and
`RMAX` are the lower/upper local-x profile bounds in metres and `GAPWIDTH` is
the transit-time width in metres. Position the gap plane at local z=0 using
`X/Y/Z/THETA/PHI/PSI`; `ANGLE` and `PDIS` must remain zero. Positive local-z
crossings receive one kick. Explicit phases are used without automatic phasing.
Time-dependent RF models and voltage/phase error attributes are not supported.

For example, before composing with the enclosing ring's pose, the old cavity at
35 degrees with 416 mm perpendicular offset has `X=0.416*sin(35 degrees)`,
`Z=-0.416*cos(35 degrees)`, and `THETA=-35*pi/180`. Subtract the ring's translation
when its axes coincide with the lab axes. More generally compose the full poses.

`sandbox/cyclotron/compare_acceleration_turn.py` generates the complete translated
input from the recorded old-OPAL launch state and runs one directed accelerating
turn. It requires the corresponding old baseline from `run_old_acceleration.py`.
The timestep defaults to 41.13 ps (2880 steps per nominal RF revolution).
All comparison runs use one MPI rank. The experimental event path evaluates
magnetic fields on the host at substeps; GPU acceleration and multi-particle
event tracking are not yet validated.

## Stop at a kinetic-energy target

For an accelerating ring, specify `EKINSTOP` on `TRACK`, in **GeV of kinetic
energy**, not total energy. For example, in a configured ring input:

```text
TRACK, LINE=MYCYCL, BEAM=BEAM0,
       DT=4.113195129976966e-11, MAXSTEPS=633600, EKINSTOP=0.590;
RUN, METHOD="PARALLEL", FIELDSOLVER=FS0;
ENDTRACK;
```

The first complete reference-particle RF kick reaching or exceeding the target
ends tracking. The last output contains the post-kick state at the gap time;
the remaining drift is omitted. Energy is **not** clamped to 590 MeV. For the
no-trim-coil reference at this timestep the recorded energy is about 590.327 MeV.

The target must be finite, positive and above the launch energy. Use one positive
`DT` segment and no explicit `RUN,TURNS`; directed turns are still reported as
diagnostics. Restart and multi-container/multi-rank runs are not supported.
`MAXSTEPS` is a hard safety limit in energy-stop mode: reaching it or leaving
magnetic field support before the target is an error, not successful completion.
Unlike the directed-turn mode, this mode does not enlarge the requested step budget.

### Reproducing the 72 to 590 MeV comparison

Run from the OPALX source root with the Python scientific dependencies available
and `omp-build/src/opalx` built. Output directories must be new. The old-OPAL
runner sources `/Users/adelmann/OPAL-2022.1/etc/profile.d/opal.sh` and launches
the installed executable directly on one rank; adapt that installation path for
another machine.

```sh
python sandbox/cyclotron/run_old_acceleration.py --no-trim-coils \
  --nominal-turns 220 --target-mev 590 \
  --output sandbox/cyclotron/validation590/old
python sandbox/cyclotron/compare_acceleration_turn.py --no-trim-coils \
  --target-mev 590 \
  --reference sandbox/cyclotron/validation590/old/to-target.csv \
  --output sandbox/cyclotron/validation590/opalx-stop
```

For coordinate comparisons, additionally use `--fixed-steps` with the step from
the old run's `target.json` (545799 in the 2880-step reference). This disables
`EKINSTOP` for that comparison run and matches old OPAL's end-of-step sample;
raw gap-stop and end-of-step positions are different physical times. Use
`--steps-per-turn 5760` in both runners for the half-timestep comparison.

### Trim coils in old-OPAL comparisons

Use `--no-trim-coils` in both runners for the baseline. Omit it in both for the
named mirrored-coil comparison. The legacy generator explicitly sets
`PHIMIN=0, PHIMAX=360`: OPAL 2022.1's PHIMAX help advertises 360 degrees, but
its constructor supplies no default value, so relying on the omission can leave
the coil inactive. A nonzero BMAX alone is not proof that the old coil was active.

The compared named model has shape radii 4.350/4.470 m, BMAX=1.4 mT and
SLPTC=600 inverse metres (old input: 4350/4470 mm and 0.6 inverse millimetres).
This is an explicit common model, not a blanket compatibility claim for obsolete
inline `TCR1/TCR2/MBTC/SLPTC` syntax. The original supplied input remains unchanged.

See [cyclotron field physics](../physics/cyclotron.qmd) for coordinate and
interpolation conventions.

## Spectral coasting tunes

`RUN,SPECTRALTUNES=TRUE` selects a separate, serial two-ray diagnostic. It reuses
the external-field ray tracker, not the linear-map construction. The physical
bunch is not tracked in this mode; its normal BEAM/source setup is still required
to initialize the lattice and particle species. Only one proton beam, one MPI
rank, a non-restarted RING containing only CYCLOTRONSECTOR elements, and
FIELDSOLVER TYPE=NONE are supported. No RF or global particle processes are allowed.

Add repeated triples to BEAM, with **kinetic energy in GeV, radius in metres,
and radial momentum in units of mc**:

```text
BEAM0: BEAM, PARTICLE=PROTON, NALLOC=1,
       BCHARGE=1.602176634e-19, SOURCES=SOURCES0, CHARGE=1,
       TUNEINITIAL={0.072,2.1314,-0.000240,
                    0.074,2.1551,-0.000296};
TRACK, LINE=MYCYCL, BEAM=BEAM0, MAXSTEPS=72000,
       DT=1.64527805199081e-10, STEPSPERTURN=720;
RUN, METHOD="PARALLEL", FIELDSOLVER=FS0, SPECTRALTUNES=TRUE,
     TURNS=100, TUNESAMPLE=50, TUNEINTEGRATOR="RK4", TUNESECTOR="SM0";
ENDTRACK;
```

Each triple launches an independent reference ray and a second ray displaced
5 mm radially and vertically, with identical initial momentum. `TUNESECTOR`
supplies the centre, entrance radial plane and coordinate orientation; it defaults
to SM0. There is no closed-orbit solve: the supplied radius/pr must be appropriate
for the energy. All rows use the same configured sector fields and trim coils.

`TURNS * STEPSPERTURN` is the number of fixed timesteps **per row** and must not
exceed MAXSTEPS. In this legacy-compatible diagnostic, TURNS means nominal turns,
not the directed-return stopping criterion of normal tracking. TUNESAMPLE is the
sampling stride (default 50). TUNEINTEGRATOR selects RK4 (default), BORIS/LF2, or
fixed-step DOP853 independently of the map integrator. EKINSTOP cannot be combined
with this mode. Linear-map computation is bypassed.

Outputs are `<base>-tunes.csv`, plus `<base>-tune-<row>-samples.csv` and
`<base>-tune-<row>-spectrum.csv`. Row indices start at zero. The summary includes
peak tunes, frequency-grid spacing, sample count, legacy normalization count and
maximum relative kinetic-energy drift. Sample output includes accumulated reference
angle, so nominal and geometric revolution counts can be distinguished. Signals
and time are pre-step; the angle is post-step, matching the legacy turn-counter
context. Do not interpret that angle as a simultaneous signal sample.

The sandbox runner `run_spectral_tunes.py` converts ic.dat's MeV/mm/scaled-pr
columns into these input units. The supplied table currently ends at 529.993 MeV;
it must not be extrapolated silently to 590 MeV. At 72 MeV, the first comparison
reproduces old OPAL's peaks 1.155 (radial) and 0.890 (vertical). These are finite-grid,
finite-amplitude measurements, not exact linear tunes.

At 72 MeV, halving DT while doubling STEPSPERTURN and TUNESAMPLE preserves the
record duration and sample cadence. Both codes retain the same peak bins. The
maximum radial signal difference decreases from 9.28 to 0.20 micrometres and
the vertical difference from 0.525 to 0.033 micrometres. OPALX's maximum relative
energy drift decreases from 7.90e-6 to 4.39e-7. These are trajectory checks in
addition to the spectral-grid comparison, not an exact-tune accuracy claim.
